title: SEASON ZERO M3: GEAR FROM WRECKS, PILLAGERS AND KEYCARD ROOMS
why: his rulings of 11-01 (answers 46, 57, 68): machines drop gear and bigger machines have better odds, a hostile pillager drops what he wears, keycard rooms hold gear, and a raid averages 4 or 5 pieces in all. Numbers, his 26 real raids v35.38 to v37.56 (abandons left out): 13.4 containers opened a raid; killed a raid 13.5 crawlers, 4.2 sentries, 0.6 snitches, 0.15 bulwarks, 0.15 howlers, 0.7 pillagers; those kills leave 12.2 wrecks and 0.7 bodies. Taking the 00p-m3a estimate of 3 in 4 opened containers as map boxes and every body opened, about 1 wreck in 5 is searched. Boxes 10.1 x 0.34 = 3.4 pieces, wrecks about 0.45 (crawler and snitch 12 percent, sentry 25, listener 40, bulwark and howler 55, pillbox 65, warden 85 with a second at 30, the overseer and the juggernaut always one and a second at 60), pillagers 0.7 x 0.65 = 0.45 (plain 50 then 15 percent, a medium or heavy rig 70 then 30, an elite 90 then 45), keycard room boxes about 0.1 more (always one, one rarity step up): about 4.4 a raid, so the box chance stays 34 percent. The run log does not split boxes from wrecks, so the 1 in 5 is an estimate to check when the log counts them.
now: a machine wreck may hold a worn piece, more often and rarer on a bigger machine; a dead pillager body holds what he wore (0 to 2 pieces, more on a tough or elite one; he looks and fights the same); every box in a keycard room holds a piece of sound or better; all on their own dice from the raid seed and the spawn, so seed 4242 and the raid streams never move and no new wreck or body appears; one table, WORN_SRC, holds every rate
